chief_complaint: Hypertension and metabolic risk management complicated by chronic pain, migraine, and substance use disorder.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 50-year-old woman with longstanding essential hypertension (dx 2011) and obesity (BMI ≥30 since 2005) who also has prediabetes (A1c 6.2%). She reports chronic widespread pain and intractable migraine since the early 1990s, and a dependent drug‑abuse disorder diagnosed in 2014 with two resolved overdoses (2020, 2024). Recent records show increasing psychosocial stress, social isolation, and persistent transportation barriers, limiting outpatient follow‑up. Only hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg is prescribed; no antihypertensive escalation, glucose‑lowering, lipid‑lowering, analgesic, or addiction‑treatment medications are documented. Visits are dominated by emergency and wellness encounters rather than regular chronic‑care visits.
past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include two drug overdoses (2020, 2024), gingivitis (resolved 2023), facial lacerations (2021), acute viral pharyngitis (2020), medication‑review reminders (2021, 2023), and prior part‑time employment (resolved 2023).
social_determinants: Limited transportation access, lack of reliable transport, social isolation, criminal record, high‑school education only, and recent transition to full‑time employment.
risk_factor_summary: Cardiovascular risk is elevated due to hypertension, obesity, prediabetes, chronic stress, and substance use. Metabolic risk is present from prediabetes and obesity. Neurologic risk from chronic migraine, musculoskeletal risk from chronic pain, and psychosocial risk from isolation and transport barriers. Available scores: A1c 6.2% (prediabetic), Charlson index 0, clinical complexity moderate. Blood pressure, BMI, lipid panel, and eGFR values are missing.
clinical_impression: Patient with uncontrolled hypertension and obesity, prediabetes, and active substance use disorder, compounded by chronic pain, migraine, psychosocial stressors, and transportation barriers, resulting in frequent emergency visits and limited chronic disease management.
